output.brief: The evidence points mainly to Callerby's own decision to move the tower crane and frame gang to Kestrel, not to Halden or its architect. The independent RFI platform shows the architect answered 62 of 64 queries on time. The two late ones were minor finishes queries from May 2026. Callerby's own drafted claim relied on the "created" date, and 39 of the 41 "late" RFIs sat in Callerby's draft status for 9–47 days before submission. The crane left in October 2025. The architect's register shows CO-09 was issued on 6 Nov, and its related RFI was answered in four days. So the design change does not explain the crane's absence through April. A small genuine change-order delay may exist, but it is unquantified. Do not submit the claim as drafted. It rests on figures the platform contradicts, and Fenmore is paid a share of anything recovered. Don't concede everything yet either. Next, get an independent delay analysis, and check the crane ledger and daily diaries for what was holding work in each period. Don't suspend the incentive scheme or discipline the superintendent. He told the truth, and punishing him would suppress information. I'm moderately confident (about 65%) in this. The main gap is how much of the delay the change orders account for.
